r3_raw: and Cenezites, the Cedmonites, 20. and the Hethits, and the Pherezits, the Raphaims also, 21. and the Amorreans and the Cananites, and Gargasites, and the Iebusites. ANNOTATIONS. CHAP. XV. 6. Believed God.] S. Hilarie (li. 9.de Trin.) and S. Ambrose-( li. r.de Abrahamam. c.3.) by this example teach vs, what manner of faith is reputed to iustice, doth simply believe that which God once saith, because he is omnipotentent, how farre soever the thing that is said surmounteth our understanding For forsoheroical was the act of Abrahams faith, promptly believing Gods word in a matter most hard to his former conceit, that for the same he receiued singular prayse; and by S. Paul The father of al that believe (Ro. 4. v.11.) where the Apostle teacheth that Abraham had no iustice, nor estimation of justice before God, until he believed in Christ (v.18.19,20.) because al workes before that faith are insufficient. Neither was this a sole faith, but had other necessarie vertues of hope, and charitie, humilitie, reverence, obcdience, and the like joyned with it. Wherefore S Iames testifieth that Abraham was iustified by workes (that is by workes following faith, not going before before faith.) For Faith (faith he) if it hane not workes, is dead in it-self, (c.2.v.17.) And by workes Abrahams faith was consummated v.22. And concludetheth thus: Doeyee see, that by workes a man is iustified, and not by faith only. v.24.
